title: bug: wrapper attribution snapshot fingerprints a symlink by its target's content, not the link text git commits
description: The snapshot hash (scripts/moe-agent.sh ~2729 `hash-object --stdin-paths`, ps1 ~2460) follows symlinks, while `git add` stores the link text. So retargeting a link to a file with the same content reads as unchanged, and editing a link's target reads as the link changing. (Before task-b62c9fc7, every symlink candidate also dropped as MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT.) Repro: `ln -s a l; git hash-object l` gives the hash of a's content, not of the string "a". Fix: hash symlinks by their readlink text (e.g. `printf %s "$(readlink p)" | git hash-object --stdin`) in both twins.
definitionOfDone: Both wrapper twins fingerprint a symlink by its link text in the baseline snapshot and the temp-index re-hash
Postflight cases in bash and ps1 cover a symlink retarget (lands) and an unchanged symlink (stays PREEXISTING)

Bash twin fix (scripts/moe-agent.sh, LF) plus the one test that extracts moe_temp_index_build.
1. New top-level function `moe_snapshot_hash P` above git_dirty_snapshot (~2683): prints the snapshot blob of TOP-relative P; prints nothing and returns non-zero on failure.
 - Not a symlink (`[ ! -L "$MOE_TOP/$1" ]`): today's `git -C "$MOE_TOP" hash-object -- "$1" 2>/dev/null`, unchanged.
 - A symlink: `idx="$(create_secure_temp)/link-$$.idx"; rm -f "$idx"`, then `row=$(GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" git -C "$MOE_TOP" update-index --add --info-only -- "$1" 2>/dev/null && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" git -C "$MOE_TOP" ls-files -s -- ":(literal)$1" 2>/dev/null) || row=""`, then `rm -f "$idx"`; print field 2 of '<mode> <blob> <stage>\t<path>' (empty row: return 1). Never export GIT_INDEX_FILE.
 Measured at planning (git 2.43 Linux, Git for Windows 2.54): this records exactly what `git add` stores, the link text (dangling links, links to directories and spaced/Unicode names included; Windows backslashes become slashes) and writes no object.
 Comment the why (hash-object follows a link to its target's bytes: a retarget to identical bytes read as unchanged, an edit to the target as a change to the link, and a dangling link failed the whole --stdin-paths batch) and 'Twin: Get-MoeSnapshotBlob'.
 Error handling: every git call keeps the file's `|| VAR=""` form (set -e must never abort the post-flight); a failed update-index or ls-files, or a link that vanished, yields an empty result, and the scratch index is removed on every path.
2. git_dirty_snapshot: after the existing real-directory skip, a symlink is hashed on the spot with `h=$(moe_snapshot_hash "$p") || h=""` and written as `${h:-?}<TAB>$xy<TAB>$p` (keeps the '?' always-changed convention); it never joins present_paths or the batch. Declare h local; regular files and D rows are unchanged; adjust the header comment.
3. moe_temp_index_build: the mismatch re-hash becomes `rehash=$(moe_snapshot_hash "$p") || rehash=""` (the snapshot's own function, as its comment already promises); an empty re-hash still means moved (MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT). Keep the ponytail ABA note.
4. scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs:169: also extract `${bashFunction('moe_snapshot_hash')}`. Otherwise the extracted moe_temp_index_build calls a missing command, drops b.mjs for the wrong reason, and the test still passes.
Then rerun the step-1 subsets (both green now) and `node --test scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs`. Edit with the Edit tool only (see risks).

PowerShell twin fix (scripts/moe-agent.ps1: UTF-8 BOM + LF; afterwards `head -c3 | od -An -tx1` must be ef bb bf and the file must hold zero CR bytes).
1. Two top-level functions beside Get-MoeDirtySnapshot (~2416); importee-guard.ps1 AST-loads every top-level function, so it needs no change.
 - `Test-MoeSymlink([string]$FullPath)`: $true only for a SymbolicLink (to a file, a directory or nothing). Check `[IO.File]::GetAttributes($FullPath) -band [IO.FileAttributes]::ReparsePoint` first (ordinary files never pay a Get-Item), then `(Get-Item -LiteralPath $FullPath -Force -ErrorAction Stop).LinkType -eq 'SymbolicLink'`. Junctions and other reparse points keep today's handling.
 - `Get-MoeSnapshotBlob([string]$Top, [string]$Path)`: '' on any failure. Not a symlink: Invoke-MoeGit hash-object -- $Path, first line trimmed, Rc 0 only. A symlink: `$idx = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ('moe-link-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))` (must not exist beforehand: git rejects an empty index file); Invoke-MoeGit -IndexFile $idx update-index --add --info-only -- $Path, then ls-files -s -- ":(literal)$Path", field 2 of the first line. Same why-comment as the sh twin; 'Twin: moe_snapshot_hash'. Measured on a real NT symlink on this host (core.symlinks=false, PS 5.1 and pwsh 7): update-index records 120000 with the blob of the forward-slash link text (9d5a2f4...), while PowerShell's .Target keeps backslashes (005b290...). Never hash .Target.
 Error handling: Test-MoeSymlink wraps its body in try/catch and returns $false (GetAttributes throws on a missing path, measured); Get-MoeSnapshotBlob returns '' on a non-zero Rc, empty output or an exception, and removes the scratch index in a finally block (`Remove-Item -LiteralPath $idx -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`).
2. Get-MoeDirtySnapshot: create $hashMap before the entry loop; test `Test-MoeSymlink $full` BEFORE the Test-Path checks (Test-Path follows links: today a dangling link is recorded as a deletion 'D' and a link to a directory is skipped as a directory). A symlink: $blob = '' and, when Get-MoeSnapshotBlob returns a blob, `$hashMap[(Get-MoePathKey $p)] = <blob>`; it never joins $toHash. The existing record loop then skips an unreadable one (this twin's convention).
3. Build-MoeTempIndexTree (~3642): `$rehash = Get-MoeSnapshotBlob $Top $c.Path; $match = ($rehash -and $rehash -eq $c.Blob)`; an empty re-hash still means moved. Never pass $IndexFile.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(A) The task's suggestion, `printf %s "$(readlink p)" | git hash-object --stdin`. It is exact on Linux and macOS, but the ps1 twin has no safe byte pipe to git: PowerShell re-encodes native stdin and appends a newline. PowerShell's .Target also keeps Windows backslashes while git stores forward slashes (measured on a real NT symlink: 005b290 vs git's 9d5a2f4), so each twin would need its own normalization. (B) CHOSEN: `git update-index --add --info-only --

` into a throwaway index, then `ls-files -s`. This is git's own add path (lstat, readlink, Git for Windows' slash normalization), so the blob is byte-identical to what `git add` stores on every platform. It writes no object and is the same code in both twins. (C) A hand-rolled SHA-1 of 'blob \0' in .NET. Rejected: object-format-specific, and it duplicates git. Tests: a separate CAS-seam scenario was folded into AD as a 4th variant (`link`), because AD's assertions are exactly the contract the re-hash must keep. AE is the only new scenario.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- sh git_dirty_snapshot (~2693) batches `hash-object --stdin-paths`. Today a dangling link, or a link to a directory, fails the whole batch: every path is then re-hashed one by one and the link gets '?' (always changed).
- ps1 Get-MoeDirtySnapshot (~2418) uses Test-Path, which follows links. A dangling link is recorded as deletion 'D'; a link to a directory is skipped as a directory.
- The mismatch re-hash (sh moe_temp_index_build ~4064, ps1 Build-MoeTempIndexTree ~3642) came from b62c9fc7 for CRLF. It must be the snapshot's own hash function.
- scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs:169 extracts moe_temp_index_build by name and runs it standalone. scripts/tests/importee-guard.ps1 AST-loads every top-level ps1 function.
- CI runs postflight.sh on Linux, and postflight.ps1 on windows-latest (PS 5.1 + pwsh, as admin, so symlinks work), through scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs. That runner fails the run on any output line starting with 'SKIP'.
- postflight.ps1's scope block runs under ErrorActionPreference Continue (~1539-3957).
- Both wrappers print `[skip] <path> <code>`; scenario L asserts on that.
- No doc describes the snapshot hashing, so no docs change.
planningNotes.risks:
- This host cannot create Windows symlinks (measured 2026-10-25).
  - PS 5.1 New-Item SymbolicLink fails with 'Administrator privilege required', and Developer Mode is off.
  - WSL `ln -s` on /mnt/d makes LX reparse points (0xA000001D) that Windows cannot read.
  - So the ps1 AE and AD-link cases skip locally and run only in CI.
  - The step-5 NVIDIA-symlink smoke is the local evidence for the ps1 branch. Never claim a ps1 symlink-case pass you did not run.
- CONTESTED FILES.
  - scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} are ASSERTED by parked task-07474ee4's old checkpoint commits (9f2cce3). postflight.{sh,ps1} and moe-agent.* are PLANNED by parked 07474ee4 and BLOCKED c2cb5cf7.
  - Under attribution.contested=skip-untouched, a contested path lands only with a TOOL witness. So make every edit with Claude's Edit/Write tools, in the session that lands it: no sed, heredoc or apply_patch writes.
  - A seat without Edit/Write must not start editing. It should call report_blocked and ask for a Claude seat (c2cb5cf7 is the open bug).
- task-5f3960df (WORKING) is editing postflight.sh's [accounts] fixture. This task dependsOn it, so start from its landed version.
- The ps1 files are UTF-8 with a BOM and LF line endings. Edits must not drop the BOM or add CR bytes.
- Runtimes: the sh harness takes ~10 min from a native-fs snapshot (~45 min from /mnt/d). Each ps1 engine takes ~12 min.
- Out of scope; these ceilings stay unchanged:
  - the ABA window in the re-hash;
  - a file swapped for a symlink whose link text equals the file's old bytes has the same blob id, because mode is not compared;
  - junctions keep today's handling.
